places.rationale: Nauru's consumption rests almost entirely on Australian money (the processing centre and the 2024 Nauru Treaty), fishing licences and imported food, water and fuel. It already lived through a collapse of more than half after the phosphate and banking crash, so a patron pulling back or global shipping breaking down could do it again. Most residents live on a low coastal belt, but the raised plateau gives a retreat option that atolls lack, and Australian strategic interest makes long-run support likely.

Tuvalu is a set of atolls about 2 m above sea level, and roughly 0.4 to 0.8 m of sea-level rise by 2100 brings flooding, cyclone surges and salt in the groundwater, so whether Funafuti can afford large land reclamation decides its future more than income does. Fishing-licence and trust-fund revenue (at risk as tuna move east), the Falepili Union's migration and disaster guarantees, and possible SI-driven cheap construction make improvement the most likely outcome but leave a fat downside tail.
